newsitem.title: Indonesia: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 2.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on April 2. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Suharto has said that people who wish to see him stay in office for five more years should consider his age because he will be 77 next year. General elections are scheduled for May 29 and the presidential election will be held in 1998.

Indonesia has started implementing new custom procedures which involve self-assessment of import duties and taxes by importers, selective on-arrival inspections and post-release audits at Jakarta's Tanjung Priok port and Soekarno-Hatta airport.

Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister I.B. Sudjana said the government could not take action against Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd, which said it had overstated the amount of gold in the Busang property in East Kalimantan, because no contracts of work had been signed.

Chief Justice Sarwata has denied allegations that the government had asked the Supreme Court to dismiss all lawsuits filed by the ousted leader of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), Megawati Sukarnoputri.
